title: SDLC controls component map
description: The declared topology of a repository: which paths belong to which component, how critical each one is, and the map-wide escalation defaults. This is the tool's INPUT, authored by a human or generated by a caller, unlike evidence/0 and policy-binding/0 which it emits. A declared-topology approximation of blast radius, never a computed dependency graph.
x-stability: Major version 0 while the binary is 0.x. Fields may be added in any release, and additionalProperties is left open at every extension point so a generator targeting this schema keeps validating against a newer binary. Removing a field, renaming one, or narrowing what one means bumps the major to component-map/1. The criticality scale is closed because the algorithm fixes it. See docs/contract.md.

schema_version.description: The format this file is written in. Optional, and absent means component-map/0 — every map written before the format was published omits it. It exists so a map written for a later format is refused by an older binary rather than read on a guess, because a misread map under-tiers silently. NOT the same field as `version` below.

version.description: Revision of the declared topology, chosen by whoever maintains the map. Recorded in evidence as map_version, which with binding_used is what lets a past tier be reproduced. Bump it when the topology changes. This is content, not format: see `schema_version` above.

components.description: Every declared component. At least one: a map declaring none can never match a path, so the engine rejects it rather than tiering everything through the unmatched-path floor.

criticality.description: Declared blast-radius class, mapped onto the tier scale as low=T0, medium=T1, high=T2, critical=T3. Closed on purpose: the algorithm fixes this scale, so an unrecognised value is a typo. The engine fails such a value safe to the top of the scale rather than the bottom, and rejects it at load time.

defaults.description: Map-wide knobs the tier algorithm reads.

unmatched_path_tier.description: Fail-safe floor applied when a changed path matches no component. Omitted defaults to high: an undeclared path is precisely the case the map cannot reason about, so it fails safe rather than open.

breadth_threshold.description: Affected-component count at which the change escalates one tier for breadth. 0 disables the rule.

id.description: Identifier for the component, unique within the map. Appears in affected_set and in the reason list, so it is read by people long after the change.

match.description: Path globs, matched against the repository-relative paths a diff names. `*` and `?` stay within one path segment; `**` crosses separators. At least one: a component with no patterns could never be affected, which reads as a declaration and behaves as nothing.

shared.description: Whether other components depend on this one. Escalates the tier by one when set. A boolean stand-in for what is really a fan-in count — a component with three dependents and one with three hundred escalate identically. See the open findings in docs/contract.md.

owners.description: Owning teams or handles. Recorded in the evidence when a tier requires an owning-team reviewer, and never verified by this tool: expanding a handle into members needs a forge API. Naming owners here makes the warning name them; it does not make the check happen.

cross_repo_consumers.description: Consumers outside this repository. Raises a warning that downstream impact is not in this diff. Inert for tiering: it does not move the tier and must not be used to smuggle in a fan-in count, which would produce a record that cites a number and a tier that ignored it.

x-engine-enforced: Two rules this schema cannot express, both checked by core.ValidateMap and both a hard load-time error: component ids must be unique within the map, and an unrecognised schema_version is refused rather than read as component-map/0.
